📌 LONDON, IRNA – Iran’s Embassy in London says Tehran has established a temporary safe maritime corridor in the Strait of Hormuz and officially notified the International Maritime Organization (IMO), warning that the United States is threatening the security of the strategic waterway by violating the war termination memorandum.

The embassy said in a post on X that the Islamic Republic of Iran, within the framework of implementing the memorandum of understanding, has officially established a temporary safe and secure maritime corridor free of technical and military obstacles.
​
The embassy said the corridor was formally communicated to the International Maritime Organization through notice S14/2026.
​
Meanwhile, the embassy said the United States, which has done nothing but violate the memorandum of understanding since the first day, is steering vessels toward a dangerous parallel route in the south.
​
The embassy said this route is not only legally questionable but also unsafe, unreliable and prone to incidents.
​
In addition to the threats, the embassy said US military aggression, including attacks on Iran’s port infrastructure and maritime monitoring towers, has turned the Strait of Hormuz into a tense and high-risk area for maritime traffic.
​
In the message, the embassy said those responsible for creating this hazardous situation must reconsider their positions if they genuinely seek safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, adding that security is a two-way path.
​
The United States has violated the war termination memorandum of understanding since July 7 through repeated attacks on Iran, which Tehran considers the primary source of fresh tensions in the Persian Gulf.
​
Iran maintains that the security of the strategic waterway can only be guaranteed within a framework of respect for the sovereignty of littoral states, compliance with international maritime regulations, and coordination with arrangements announced by Tehran and Muscat.
​
Iran has repeatedly stated that maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz cannot be achieved through unilateral action and political pressure, and that parties seeking safe passage must abandon efforts to escalate tensions and violate existing understandings.

🖥 Yemen says Saudi strike on Sanaa airport ends de-escalation phase

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Yemen’s armed forces say that Saudi Arabia’s air strikes on Sanaa International Airport marked the end of a period of de-escalation, warning that the attacks would not go unanswered.

In a statement carried by the Al Masirah television network on Monday, military spokesperson Yahya Saree condemned the strikes as a “clear and unjust aggression” and said the Saudi government would bear full responsibility for the consequences.
​
Saree said Yemen’s armed forces would respond to the attacks, adding that the strikes “will not go unanswered or unpunished.”
​
The statement followed media reports that air strikes had targeted Sanaa International Airport, with the runway reportedly hit several times.
​
A member of the political bureau of Yemen's Ansarullah movement also warned that any response to Saudi aggression will be direct and decisive.
​
Mohammed Al-Furah, a member of the Ansarullah political bureau, said the response to any direct aggression by Saudi Arabia or its proxy forces will be direct, decisive, and will reach deep inside Saudi Arabia.
